title: Dillon Brooks has surgery on fractured hand, adding to Suns’ mounting injury woes
content:
PHOENIX — The Phoenix Suns might be the NBA’s most surprising team, but injuries are testing their resolve, not to mention their depth.

Forward Dillon Brooks had surgery Monday to repair a fracture in his left hand, an injury suffered early in Saturday’s home win over Orlando, and the defensive-minded forward will be re-evaluated in four to six weeks, the Suns announced Tuesday.

In addition, star guard Devin Booker remains out with a right hip strain, and bench energizer Jordan Goodwin is out with a left calf strain. Booker is expected to be re-evaluated soon. Goodwin will be re-evaluated in one to two weeks.

The Suns host the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night.

Brooks’ absence is a significant problem, not just because of the injury’s severity — a six-week recovery could last until April — but because of his value. Along with Goodwin, Brooks has been the power source behind Phoenix’s reversal, a team playing with toughness and grit. Entering Tuesday, Phoenix’s 112.5 defensive rating ranked eighth in the league.

Brooks also has been a top offensive option, averaging a career-best 20.9 points. With Jalen Green out for much of the first half of the season, his aggressiveness was a reason the Suns surged to 11 games over .500 at the end of January, but much has changed. As his teammates struggled in Sunday’s home loss to Portland, Brooks watched from the bench, his left hand wrapped in a brace, a symbol of where the Suns stand with 24 games remaining.

“Next man up, really,” second-year forward Ryan Dunn said after the Portland loss. “Guys having to step into a different role, just growing and learning at this point. We have a lot of guys out.”

The Suns put up a season-low 77 points against Portland, a game in which they also did not have steady guard Grayson Allen, who was held out for right knee and ankle management. At 33-25, the Suns are in seventh place in the West, but they have slipped this month, losing six of nine.

The limited manpower has forced coach Jordan Ott to try different combinations and lineups. Against Portland, rookie center Khaman Maluach, the 10th pick of last year’s draft, played a season-high 16 minutes, posting seven points and seven rebounds. Fellow rookie and versatile defender Rasheer Fleming played a season-high 22 minutes.

Booker, Brooks, Allen and Green — the group expected to provide the bulk of this season’s scoring — have played together in only three games this season because of injuries. Green, slowed with a hamstring injury, has played in only 10 contests and is still working to increase his confidence and conditioning.

Green struggled in Saturday’s double-overtime win over the Orlando Magic but hit the winning 3-pointer as time expired. In Sunday’s loss to Portland, the explosive guard played only 22 minutes because it was his first back-to-back of the season. Green shot 12-of-42 in those contests, missing 15 of 18 from 3-point range.

“I think I’m getting pretty close,” Green said. “Going out there without thinking about anything or being cautious in general.”

Booker’s expected return, along with Allen’s, should help. Although Booker’s efficiency has dipped this season — he’s shooting a career-low 30.8 percent from 3 — he remains Phoenix’s catalyst. Everything works better offensively with the five-time All-Star on the floor. He not only averages 24.7 points (14th in the league), but he also gets to the foul line 7.9 times per game (tied for sixth). He also draws double teams and finds open teammates.

With Booker injured, everything gets complicated.

Booker initially sprained his right ankle in the second half of a Jan. 23 loss at Atlanta. That injury kept him sidelined eight of Phoenix’s next 10 games, a stretch in which the Suns went 5-5. After participating in the All-Star weekend, Booker returned and injured his hip in last Thursday’s loss against the San Antonio Spurs.

An example of how Booker’s absence affects the Suns: Forward Royce O’Neale is one of Phoenix’s top shooters, making 39.7 percent of his 3-point attempts this season. But over the 10 contests Booker recently missed, O’Neale made 19 of 69 from deep (27.5 percent).

“This is not just a one-night thing,” Ott said. “We’ve struggled to score for an extended period of time. Our shot quality has not been good. We’ll continue to try and figure it out.”
